tutor.guide:
CREATE A PROJECT
Open [23] Workspace → n → c, then name the project.
Press p to choose its input file. An HTTP log or a PCAP is enough.
Press a to add text references, then Enter to create the project.

CHOOSE A FILE
Use ↑/↓ to select, → or Enter to open, and ← or Backspace to go up a folder.
Use d for Downloads, ~ for home, w for the working folder, or t to type/paste a path.

ANALYZE
HTTP log: g opens the full reader. In categories, [LOG] actions run directly on the file.
PDF: attach a PDF under Workspace → u → a, then open category [18].
PCAP: open a category, select an action, then press Enter to run TShark.
Use e for the command explanation, a for refinements, and x to export the result.

WORKSPACE
u lists references, y opens history, and Enter switches between English and Portuguese.

FILTER EXAMPLES FOR PCAP
  tcp.port == 443
  frame.time_relative >= 10 && frame.time_relative <= 60

LOG TO TSHARK
[19.19] generates a derived capture. Press o after conversion to use it.
[19.20] preserves log bytes as text payload. Read them with [19.21] and a → d.

COMMAND EDITOR
[3.7], [2.2] and [4.6]: a adjusts, t edits output stages, h explains, c copies.
Press B during a run to continue in the background.

editor.generic_help:
[e] explains the preset. [a] shows filters and output settings available to this action.
[Enter] runs it on the active project input. [x] exports results. [Esc] returns.
editor.shared_help:
EDIT AND RUN
Enter executes the current preview. a edits filters or display settings. t manages output steps.
The input comes from the project. Use p on the action screen to change it.
Only the TShark filter changes which packets match. Output steps process the rows TShark returns.
c opens the full command and c again sends it to the terminal clipboard. s saves, b reloads and R restores.
For more examples press F1 from the action screen.
editor.syn_ports_summary: Counts observed TCP SYN packets per destination port. Default: ten most frequent ports.
editor.synack_summary: Counts observed TCP SYN+ACK packets by the source IPv4 or IPv6 address.
editor.payload_summary: Shows TCP payload with source address and ports. Adjust port, direction, PSH and decoding with a.
editor.syn_ports_help:
WHAT IT READS
The display filter selects TCP SYN with ACK clear. The field tcp.dstport is the destination port.
Use a → 1 and a → 2 to narrow to source and destination IP.

HOW THE RESULT IS BUILT
sort -n groups equal port numbers. uniq -c counts adjacent duplicates. sort -rn orders by frequency. head -n 10 keeps the first ten lines.
Each count represents packets. Retransmitted SYNs can appear again.
editor.synack_help:
The display filter selects packets with both SYN and ACK set. The source address is the host that sent each reply.
The first awk step chooses IPv4 or IPv6. sort and uniq -c count replies per address; sort -rn puts the highest counts first.
Use a → 1 and a → 2 to narrow the addresses. The result reflects packets seen, including unrelated replies unless the filter excludes them.
editor.payload_help:
The preset reads tcp.payload per segment. a → p sets the TCP port. Reopen a and use r to choose to-port or from-port, u for PSH, and d for text.
To port uses tcp.dstport; from port uses tcp.srcport. Both accepts either direction.
Decoding prints the source address and source → destination ports before each line. Use a stream action if you need TCP reassembly.
